A cathedral-vast hall of towering wooden shelves climbing dozens of stories into shadow, narrow galleries and spiral stairs winding between them, the ceiling lost in gloom far above.
An endless spiral-tower of book-stacks winding up and out of sight, a dizzying central void dropping away below, warm lamplight glowing at every level.
A grand star-domed reading-room ringed by tiers of book-galleries, a painted constellation ceiling glowing faintly above, long tables far below.
A forbidden archive of chained tomes stacked floor to vaulted ceiling, iron walkways bolted into crumbling stone, the uppermost shelves swallowed entirely by darkness and cold damp air.
A sunlit hall of soaring marble columns with shelves packed between each pillar rising six stories high, clerestory windows flooding the upper galleries in amber afternoon light.
A labyrinth of narrow towering stacks pressing close on every side, shelves climbing thirty feet overhead, flickering sconces casting restless shadows across the tight suffocating aisles between.
A circular library built around a central well dropping into unfathomable dark below, shelves ringing every level of the shaft, ladders descending past dim lanterns into silence.
A hall of floating bookshelves drifting silently at every altitude from floor to vaulted apex, connected by rope bridges swaying gently, the highest shelves nearly invisible in amber haze.
An ancient ruined library reclaimed by ivy and moss, shelves still standing beneath a collapsed roof open to sky, towers of rotting books reaching toward drifting clouds above.

A gothic vaulted scriptorium of ribbed stone arches soaring overhead, tall narrow shelves filling every bay between the pillars, candlelight trembling across tiers of illuminated manuscripts far above.
A crystal-walled library glowing with cold inner light, shelves climbing inside translucent walls to a dizzying apex, every book visible through the luminous facets as tiny dark rectangles.
A library carved entirely into a coastal cliff-cavern, tiers of rock-hewn shelves rising fifty feet to the rough ceiling, lanterns hung on chains swaying with the sea wind.
A drowned archive beneath a glass-vaulted reservoir, shelves standing in shallow water, fish drifting between the upper tiers, diffuse green light filtering down from the surface far overhead.
An obsidian tower-library of black stone shelves climbing without apparent end, firefly-like magelight drifting at every level, the topmost stacks wrapped in a permanent cloud of pale mist.
A vast mechanical library of rotating iron shelves operated by clicking gears, rising ten stories to a copper-domed ceiling, the whole structure rumbling and shifting in slow grinding rotation.
A desert-temple library open to blazing sky above, shelves cut into sandstone walls climbing forty feet, falcon shadows crossing the sun-bleached papyrus scrolls stacked in every niche overhead.
A forest-canopy library built among the upper boughs of ancient trees, rope-and-plank shelves ascending through the branches, the highest reading platforms swaying in open sky above the leaves.
A frozen polar archive of ice-carved shelves climbing a glacial cavern, books sealed in translucent ice blocks stacked to a vaulted frost-ceiling, cold blue light suffusing every level.
A subterranean library of vast natural caverns linked by rope bridges, shelves covering every rock wall from floor to stalactite ceiling fifty feet above, echoes of dripping water everywhere.
A celestial observatory-library of nested rotating galleries ascending a brass tower, star-charts and tomes shelved together at every tier, the topmost platform open to wheeling night sky.
A mirrored hall of infinite reflected shelves, each wall a perfect mirror multiplying the towering stacks into endless false depth, the real ceiling invisible among its thousand reflections above.
A volcanic library carved into basalt columns inside a dormant caldera, shelves ascending the hexagonal stone walls to a ring of open sky far overhead, heat shimmering upward.
A monastery archive of whitewashed walls lined floor to vaulted ceiling with plain wooden shelves, narrow iron-railed galleries at every story, a single shaft of dusty light falling through.
A cloud-citadel library suspended above the world, shelves filling rooms that open onto one another through archways climbing higher, the topmost chamber simply a floor open to open sky.
A ruined colosseum converted to a library, shelves filling every tier of the great oval rising six stories, open to stars through the broken upper arcade, wind moving the pages.
